essence: Body catalogued as delusion's house; knowing and unknowing alike plunged for not knowing her greatness.
Installed images leave seers unfulfilled: body-I-ness breeds every delusion.
Protection-begging from the all born of delusion-play: effort-born self-awareness as the guard against falling.
Beholding the manifold power — terrible and not — ends in wonder-abiding, not doctrine.
Mid-ray dwelling dissolves insistence: no grip on any being-nonbeing judgment.
Both forms remembered together: unsurpassed and world-made — to the good, fear and boon from one goddess.
Double petition: lift the fallen fettered one; soothe the child — cool glances for heat.
Lineage-bow then authorship claim: perfected ones first, then the fifteen verses as Abhinavagupta's uttering.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta settling toward śānta (wonder worked into rest)
rasa.justification: The body inventoried tissue by tissue, delusion named and refused, power beheld until beholding stills: praise that begins in the senses ends in cool glances and a bowed head.

sections.FUNCTION: Contemplates the body as delusion's house, refuses the set-up gods, and closes with petition and bowed head.
sections.KEY TERMS: māhātmya (greatness as what the plunged do not know); lohālekhya (metal-drawn images as unfulfilling); ātma-vimarśa (self-awareness as guard); vismaya (wonder as beholding's end); abhidā (being-nonbeing judgments as released grip); kaṭākṣa (cool glances as grace).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Surrender made, throbbing meditated: now the body inventoried, images refused, protection begged, power wondered at, judgments dropped, both forms held, child soothed, line bowed to.
sections.BOUNDARY: No siddhi is claimed; petition stays open-ended.
sections.RELATED: Dyczkowski per-verse exposition (petal structure generalized to sense-offerings here); Sharada ms different transmission — noted, not collated; v16 attribution to Abhinavagupta — ending in his own name.
sections.EXPLANATION: The second movement inventories the body tissue by tissue — skin to marrow — and names it delusion’s house, into which knowing and unknowing alike are plunged for not knowing her greatness. Set-up gods in metal leave their seers unfulfilled: with body-I-ness intact, every delusion is mothered. So protection is begged from the all born of delusion-play, with effort-born self-awareness as guard. Then beholding itself: terrible, most terrible, non-terrible — manifold power watched until the watcher abides in wonder, holding no thesis. Mid-ray dwelling dissolves insistence: no grip left on any being or nonbeing judgment. Both her forms are remembered together — unsurpassed and world-made — dealing fear to the good and boons to the good from one goddess. The close petitions twice: lift the fallen fettered one, soothe the child with cool glances. Last, the lineage is bowed to — perfected ones, gods, goddess, yogins — and the fifteen verses stand uttered by Abhinavagupta.
